//: lib: ["ES5", "ES2015.Symbol"] is the floor this package actually needs, and the sliver above the base's ES5 is set by a single identifier: Symbol.for (single-instance-guard.ts) -- verified the inherited ["ES5"] fails on exactly that one (TS2585, 'try changing lib to es2015 or later'), and that the sliver alone clears it, so no bump to the full ["ES2015"]. Everything else here is a locally-declared interface plus `Record` and the `Symbol` type (lib.es5.d.ts), so nothing pulls in anything higher. DOM stays absent: every platform global is reached by casting `globalThis` through an owned structural type, never by naming a DOM type, and types: [] (from tsconfig.lib.json) keeps @types/node and bun-types out too. See tsconfig.compat.json for the companion no-conflict-with-real-libs program.
